# Purpose
This project examines overall trends in CTA L ridership between 1999 and 2026 and identifies how the COVID-19 pandemic may have influenced train travel--both generally and across specific lines (e.g., Green, Pink, Red) and neighborhood categories--in the City of Chicago throughout the various waves of the pandemic. The sections below step you through the process for creating tables, maps and figures to inform your presentation. *As with previous exercises, you are asked to combine and submit all materials into a single presentation. The basic template for this exercise can be downloaded [via this link to the PowerPoint slides](https://justenvirons.org/pedagogy/GEO330/Exercise_03/slides/Exercise03_Template.pptx) on the course data pages.*

The load command imports the datasets listed below, along with custom functions (all beginning with "fx_") that create the exercise's tables, plots and maps. The code for each function can be viewed by clicking the "Show" links throughout this document.

# Step 2. Explore geographic data 
This exercise evaluates L ridership and COVID-19 trends for neighborhoods in the city of Chicago. To do this, we need community areas, zip codes and L stations in a spatial (i.e., mappable) format. These datasets, and all data for this exercise, are publicly available via the [Chicago data portal](https://data.cityofchicago.org/) and the Regional Transportation Authority's Mapping and Statistics [(RTAMS)](https://rtams.org/) websites. CTA rail stations and lines were downloaded from the *Shapefiles and Feature Layers* section of the [RTAMS Maps and Data web page](https://rtagis.maps.arcgis.com/home/index.html).

## L stations by community area and zip code
It is necessary to attribute L stations with community areas and zip codes in order to evaluate CCVI and COVID-19 cases with ridership trends. That is, ridership is reported by L station whereas CCVI and COVID-19 cases are reported by community area and zip code. Therefore each L station in the `rail_stations` dataset was associated with its nearest community area and zip code using a spatial join. @fig-stationbycomareazip below tabulates L stations by community area and zip code.

```{r}
#| label: define station table functions
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the station table functions"

# function for formatting a table as an interactive table
fx_datatable <- function(table) {
  datatable(table,
            class = 'cell-border stripe',
            rownames = FALSE,
            options = list(pageLength = 5),
            filter = "top")
}

# function for tabulating L stations by community area and zip code
fx_table_stations <- function(rail_stations) {
  rail_stations %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    select(`L Station` = station_name,
           `Community Area` = comarea_name,
           `Station Line` = station_line,
           `Zip Code` = zip) %>%
    arrange(`L Station`) %>%
    fx_datatable()
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-stationbycomareazip
#| fig-cap: L Station by Community Area and Zip Code

# tabulate L stations by community area and zip code
fx_table_stations(rail_stations)

```

## CCVI by Chicago community area
We will be evaluating L ridership based on a variety of community characteristics included in the Chicago COVID-19 Community Vulnerability Index (CCVI). The index was adapted and modified from [Surgo Ventures](https://precisionforcovid.org/ccvi) and the [CDC Social Vulnerability Index](https://www.atsdr.cdc.gov/placeandhealth/svi/index.html) to identify communities (i.e., both community areas and zip codes) in Chicago that have been disproportionately impacted by COVID-19. Vulnerability is defined as a combination of: sociodemographic factors; epidemiological factors; occupational factors and other factors related to cumulative COVID burden. These factors are combined and weighted to create a single composite CCVI score. The higher the score, the more vulnerable the geographic area or, in this case, community area. The `community_areas_ccvi` dataset joins the CCVI scores, categories and ranks (from least (1) to most (77) vulnerable) to community areas.

## Create map showing CCVI distribution by community area 
R has several packages devoted to map making. The *leaflet* package can be used to create custom, interactive maps (@fig-ccvibycommunityarea). Modify the color palette ([see this reference for palette names](https://i0.wp.com/1.bp.blogspot.com/-3VQwNXWga9s/UICXF7rbvLI/AAAAAAAAAUg/UQBmpUO9kVA/s1600/display-brewer-all.png)) in the code below to create a custom map showing variations by CCVI category. Use the "Map" dropdown list in the upper right of the map to switch between CCVI category and quintiles of selected CCVI ranks (from least to most vulnerable), and the checkboxes below it to turn L lines and stations on and off. Hover over community areas and stations for more details. Insert the map into slide 1 of your presentation.

```{r}
#| label: define CCVI mapping functions
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the CCVI mapping functions"

# function for creating the base map shared by the exercise's maps: CARTO
# basemap, reset and full screen buttons and community area boundaries for
# reference (added first, so they are drawn beneath the other layers)
fx_basemap <- function(map_data, carto_api_key = CARTO_API_KEY) {
  leaflet(data = st_transform(map_data, crs = 4326)) %>%
    addTiles(urlTemplate = paste0(
      "https://basemaps.cartocdn.com/rastertiles/light_all/{z}/{x}/{y}.png?key=",
      carto_api_key
    )) %>%
    addResetMapButton() %>%
    addFullscreenControl() %>%
    addPolygons(
      fill = FALSE,
      color = "#555",
      weight = 1,
      opacity = 1)
}

# function for creating community area hover labels with CCVI scores, categories
# and ranks
fx_ccvi_labels <- function(community_areas_ccvi) {
  x <- community_areas_ccvi
  sprintf(
    "<strong>%s</strong><br/>
    <i>CCVI Score:</i> %0.1f<br/>
    <i>CCVI Category:</i> %s<br/><br/>
    <em>Ranked scores from least (1) to most (77) vulnerable:</em><br/>
    <i>Socioeconomic Status:</i> %1.0f<br/>
    <i>Essential Workers:</i> %1.0f<br/>
    <i>Mobility Ratio:</i> %1.0f<br/>
    <i>COVID-19 Incidence Rate:</i> %1.0f<br/>
    <i>COVID-19 Hospitalization Rate:</i> %1.0f<br/>
    <i>COVID-19 Crude Mortality Rate:</i> %1.0f<br/>",
    x$comarea_name,
    x$`CCVI Score`,
    x$`CCVI Category`,
    x$`Rank - Socioeconomic Status`,
    x$`Rank - Frontline Essential Workers`,
    x$`Rank - Cumulative Mobility Ratio`,
    x$`Rank - COVID-19 Incidence Rate`,
    x$`Rank - COVID-19 Hospital Admission Rate`,
    x$`Rank - COVID-19 Crude Mortality Rate`) %>%
    lapply(htmltools::HTML)
}

# function for adding one community area layer and legend per measure, plus a
# dropdown list (top right) that shows one measure at a time; the first measure
# is shown when the map opens. measures and pals are named lists of values and
# their color palettes.
fx_add_measure_layers <- function(map, map_data, measures, pals, labels) {
  for (i in seq_along(measures)) {
    values <- measures[[i]]
    pal <- pals[[i]]
    map <- map %>%
      addPolygons(
        data = map_data,
        fillColor = pal(values),
        label = labels,
        weight = 2,
        opacity = 1,
        color = "white",
        dashArray = "3",
        fillOpacity = 0.7,
        group = names(measures)[i]) %>%
      addLegend("bottomleft",
                pal = pal,
                values = values,
                title = names(measures)[i],
                opacity = 1,
                className = paste0("info legend measure-legend measure-legend-", i - 1))
  }
  map %>%
    htmlwidgets::onRender("
      function(el, x, data) {
        var map = this;
        var groups = [].concat(data.groups);
        // show the selected measure's layer and legend and hide the others
        function show(i) {
          groups.forEach(function(g, j) {
            var layer = map.layerManager.getLayerGroup(g, false);
            if (layer) {
              if (j === i) { map.addLayer(layer); } else { map.removeLayer(layer); }
            }
          });
          el.querySelectorAll('.measure-legend').forEach(function(d) {
            d.style.display = d.classList.contains('measure-legend-' + i) ? '' : 'none';
          });
        }
        var control = L.control({position: 'topright'});
        control.onAdd = function() {
          var div = L.DomUtil.create('div', 'leaflet-bar');
          div.style.background = 'white';
          div.style.padding = '4px 6px';
          div.innerHTML = '<label style=\"font-weight: bold; margin-right: 4px;\">Map</label>';
          var select = L.DomUtil.create('select', '', div);
          groups.forEach(function(g, j) {
            var option = L.DomUtil.create('option', '', select);
            option.value = j;
            option.text = g;
          });
          select.onchange = function() { show(parseInt(select.value)); };
          L.DomEvent.disableClickPropagation(div);
          L.DomEvent.disableScrollPropagation(div);
          return div;
        };
        control.addTo(map);
        show(0);
      }", data = list(groups = names(measures)))
}

# function for adding L lines (colored by line) and stations; lines and stations
# are drawn in their own panes, above the community areas. station_labels are the
# stations' hover labels; other circle marker options (e.g., radius, fillColor)
# are passed through ...
fx_add_rail_layers <- function(map, rail_lines, rail_stations, station_labels, ...) {
  map %>%
    addMapPane("lines", zIndex = 440) %>%
    addMapPane("stations", zIndex = 450) %>%
    addPolylines(
      data = st_transform(rail_lines, crs = 4326),
      weight = 3,
      opacity = 1,
      color = ~unname(pal_line[COLOR]),
      options = pathOptions(pane = "lines"),
      group = "L Lines") %>%
    addCircleMarkers(
      data = st_transform(rail_stations, crs = 4326),
      color = "#fff",
      weight = 1,
      fillOpacity = 0.9,
      label = station_labels,
      options = pathOptions(pane = "stations"),
      group = "L Stations",
      ...)
}

# vulnerability quintile labels, from least to most vulnerable
vulnerability_labels <- c("Least vulnerable", "Less vulnerable", "Moderate",
                          "More vulnerable", "Most vulnerable")

# function for mapping CCVI by community area with L lines and stations; the
# dropdown list switches between CCVI category and quintiles of selected CCVI
# ranks, and the layer control turns the lines and stations on and off. palette
# is any RColorBrewer palette name (e.g., "YlOrRd", "Blues", "PuRd")
fx_map_ccvi <- function(community_areas_ccvi, rail_lines, rail_stations_ccvi, palette = "YlOrRd") {
  map_data <- st_transform(community_areas_ccvi, crs = 4326)

  # CCVI category and quintiles of selected ranks (1 = least vulnerable)
  rank_quintile <- function(column) {
    factor(vulnerability_labels[map_data[[paste0(column, "_ntile")]]], levels = vulnerability_labels)
  }
  measures <- list(
    "CCVI Category" = map_data$`CCVI Category`,
    "Socioeconomic Status Rank<br>Quintiles" = rank_quintile("Rank - Socioeconomic Status"),
    "Essential Workers Rank<br>Quintiles" = rank_quintile("Rank - Frontline Essential Workers"),
    "Mobility Ratio Rank<br>Quintiles" = rank_quintile("Rank - Cumulative Mobility Ratio"),
    "COVID-19 Incidence Rate Rank<br>Quintiles" = rank_quintile("Rank - COVID-19 Incidence Rate"),
    "COVID-19 Hospitalization Rate Rank<br>Quintiles" = rank_quintile("Rank - COVID-19 Hospital Admission Rate"),
    "COVID-19 Crude Mortality Rate Rank<br>Quintiles" = rank_quintile("Rank - COVID-19 Crude Mortality Rate"))
  pals <- lapply(measures, function(values)
    colorFactor(palette = palette, domain = values, levels = levels(values), ordered = TRUE))
  # dropdown list names without the legend line break
  names(measures) <- names(pals) <- gsub("<br>", " ", names(measures))

  # station hover labels
  station_labels <- sprintf(
    "<strong>%s</strong><br/>
    <i>Line:</i> %s<br/>
    <i>Community area:</i> %s<br/>
    <i>CCVI Category:</i> %s",
    rail_stations_ccvi$station_name,
    rail_stations_ccvi$station_line,
    rail_stations_ccvi$comarea_name,
    rail_stations_ccvi$`CCVI Category`) %>%
    lapply(htmltools::HTML)

  fx_basemap(map_data) %>%
    fx_add_measure_layers(map_data,
                          measures = measures,
                          pals = pals,
                          labels = fx_ccvi_labels(map_data)) %>%
    fx_add_rail_layers(rail_lines, rail_stations_ccvi, station_labels,
                       radius = 4,
                       fillColor = "#333") %>%
    addLayersControl(
      overlayGroups = c("L Lines", "L Stations"),
      options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE, position = "topright"))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ccvibycommunityarea
#| fig-cap: CCVI Scores by Community Area

# map CCVI by community area with L lines and stations
fx_map_ccvi(community_areas_ccvi, 
            rail_lines, 
            rail_stations_ccvi, 
            palette = "YlOrRd") # EDIT HERE

```

# Step 3. Evaluate CTA L ridership data before and during the COVID-19 pandemic
## Ridership by L station
The Regional Transportation Authority provides information on the location and performance of the three public transit operators within metropolitan Chicago, namely, PACE Suburban Bus, Chicago Transit Authority (CTA both bus and rail), and Metra commuter rail. The Chicago Data Portal also serves up daily boardings for CTA. For this exercise we focus specifically on CTA rail ridership using two datasets: (1) daily rail boardings for all L stations (`ridership_daily_boardings`, from the Chicago Data Portal); and (2) monthly boardings by L station from January 1999 through `r format(ridership_through, "%B %Y")` (`ridership_attributes`, [downloaded from RTAMS](https://rtams.org/media/datasets/cta-ridership)).

## Create plots showing ridership trends over time
The following code uses the "plotly" package to create charts showing trends in total weekday boardings by month (@fig-railboardingsmonth) between January 1999 and `r format(ridership_through, "%B %Y")` and weekday boardings by day (@fig-railboardingsdaily).

```{r}
#| label: define ridership plotting functions
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the ridership plotting functions"

# function for applying the layout shared by the exercise's plots: y axis title,
# horizontal legend below the plot, unified hover labels and an image download
# button that saves the plot as filename.png
fx_plot_layout <- function(p, y_title, filename, x_title = "") {
  p %>%
    config(displaylogo = FALSE,
           modeBarButtons = list(list("toImage", "resetScale2d")),
           toImageButtonOptions = list(filename = filename)) %>%
    layout(
      xaxis = list(title = x_title),
      yaxis = list(title = y_title),
      legend = list(
        font = list(size = 10),
        orientation = "h",
        xanchor = "center",
        x = 0.5, y = -0.1),
      hovermode = "x unified")
}

# function for plotting total boardings (all stations) by month; day_type is
# "Weekday", "Saturday" or "Sunday/Holiday"
fx_plot_ridership_by_month <- function(ridership_attributes, day_type = "Weekday") {
  ridership_by_month <- ridership_attributes %>%
    filter(day_type == !!day_type) %>%
    group_by(year_month) %>%
    summarise(rides_total = sum(rides_total), .groups = "drop")

  plot_ly(data = ridership_by_month,
          x = ~year_month,
          y = ~rides_total,
          type = 'scatter',
          mode = 'lines',
          line = list(color = "#080967", width = 0.5),
          name = 'Total boardings',
          hovertemplate = 'Rides: %{y:,}<extra></extra>') %>%
    fx_plot_layout(y_title = paste0("Total Rail Station Boardings (", day_type, ")"),
                   filename = "cta_rail_boardings_by_month")
}

# function for plotting daily rail boardings (all stations); day_type is "W"
# (weekday), "A" (Saturday) or "U" (Sunday/holiday)
fx_plot_daily_boardings <- function(ridership_daily_boardings, day_type = "W") {
  plot_ly(data = filter(ridership_daily_boardings, day_type == !!day_type),
          x = ~service_date,
          y = ~rail_boardings,
          type = 'scatter',
          mode = 'lines',
          line = list(color = "#9F1928", width = 0.5),
          name = 'Rail boardings',
          hovertemplate = 'Rail boardings: %{y:,}<extra></extra>') %>%
    fx_plot_layout(y_title = "Daily Rail Station Boardings",
                   filename = "cta_rail_boardings_by_day")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-railboardingsmonth
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Total Weekday CTA L Rail Station Boardings by Month, Chicago, Illinois, January 1999-", format(ridership_through, "%B %Y"))

# plot total weekday rail boardings per month
fx_plot_ridership_by_month(ridership_attributes, day_type = "Weekday")

```

```{r}
#| label: fig-railboardingsdaily
#| fig-cap: Weekday CTA L Rail Station Boardings by Day, Chicago, Illinois

# plot weekday rail boardings per day
fx_plot_daily_boardings(ridership_daily_boardings, day_type = "W")

```

## L stations by CCVI
The `rail_stations_ccvi` dataset joins each L station with the CCVI attributes of its community area, and the `rail_stations_ccvi_ridership` dataset adds monthly weekday boardings. These allow us to link trends in ridership by community area with CCVI scores and ranks. @fig-ccvibystation below tabulates L stations by line and CCVI.

```{r}
#| label: define station CCVI table function
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the station CCVI table function"

# function for tabulating L stations by line and CCVI
fx_table_stations_ccvi <- function(rail_stations_ccvi) {
  rail_stations_ccvi %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    select(`L Station` = station_name,
           `L Station ID` = station_id,
           `Community Area` = comarea_name,
           `Station Line` = station_line,
           `CCVI Score`,
           `CCVI Category`) %>%
    arrange(`L Station`) %>%
    fx_datatable()
}
```

```{r}

fx_table_stations_ccvi(rail_stations_ccvi)

```

## COVID-19 cases and deaths in Chicago
The Chicago data portal also makes available COVID-19 case and mortality data. Note that COVID-19 is no longer considered a notifiable disease, meaning that local health departments such as the Chicago Department of Public Health (CDPH) no longer need to report COVID-19 cases to CDC. As a result, the city's COVID-19 data reporting ended in May 2024. These data (`covid19_cases_summary`) can be plotted to identify different waves of the pandemic then compared to trends in rail usage.

Compare trends in rail ridership (above) with COVID-19 trends reported by the city of Chicago shown in the plot below (@fig-covidcases7davg). *Create a customized version of the below plot by changing the layer from 7-day average deaths (i.e., "Deaths7d") to 7-day average cases (i.e., "Cases7d").*

```{r}
#| label: define COVID-19 plotting function
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the COVID-19 plotting function"

# function for plotting COVID-19 cases or deaths by date; layer is "Cases7d" or
# "Deaths7d" (7-day averages), "Cases" or "Deaths" (daily) or "Casescm" or
# "Deathscm" (cumulative)
fx_plot_covid <- function(covid19_cases_summary, layer = "Deaths7d") {
  layer_titles <- c(Cases7d = "COVID-19 Cases (7-day average)",
                    Deaths7d = "COVID-19 Deaths (7-day average)",
                    Cases = "COVID-19 Cases",
                    Deaths = "COVID-19 Deaths",
                    Casescm = "COVID-19 Cases (cumulative)",
                    Deathscm = "COVID-19 Deaths (cumulative)")
  title <- layer_titles[[layer]]

  plot_ly(data = filter(covid19_cases_summary, layer == !!layer),
          x = ~Date,
          y = ~value,
          type = 'scatter',
          mode = 'lines',
          line = list(color = "#9F1928", width = 0.5),
          name = title,
          hovertemplate = paste0(title, ': %{y:,}<extra></extra>')) %>%
    fx_plot_layout(y_title = title,
                   filename = paste0("covid19_", tolower(layer), "_chicago"))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-covidcases7davg
#| fig-cap: COVID-19 Deaths (rolling 7-day average) by Day, Chicago Illinois

# plot COVID-19 deaths (7-day average)
fx_plot_covid(covid19_cases_summary, layer = "Deaths7d") # EDIT HERE

```

# Step 4. Examine ridership by station characteristics
@fig-ridershipbyccvi plots ridership trends by CCVI category (i.e., Low, Medium, and High) whereas @fig-ridershipbyline shows ridership by CTA L Line.

```{r}
#| label: define ridership by station characteristics functions
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the ridership by CCVI and line plotting functions"

# CCVI category colors
pal_ccvi <- c(LOW = "#E2F11A", MEDIUM = "#E0A100", HIGH = "#9F1928")

# L line colors; names match station_line and the rail lines' COLOR column
pal_line <- c(Blue = "#3498db", Brown = "#964B00", Green = "#1e8449", Multi = "#424949",
              Orange = "#e67e22", Pink = "#f5b7b1", Purple = "#7d3c98", Red = "#e74c3c",
              Yellow = "#f4d03f")

# function for plotting weekday boardings by month and station CCVI category
fx_plot_ridership_by_ccvi <- function(rail_stations_ccvi_ridership) {
  ridership_by_ccvi <- rail_stations_ccvi_ridership %>%
    drop_na(`CCVI Category`) %>%
    group_by(year_month, `CCVI Category`) %>%
    summarise(rides_total = sum(rides_total), .groups = "drop")

  plot_ly(data = ridership_by_ccvi,
          x = ~year_month,
          y = ~rides_total,
          type = 'scatter',
          mode = 'lines',
          color = ~`CCVI Category`,
          colors = pal_ccvi,
          text = ~`CCVI Category`,
          hovertemplate = '%{text}: %{y:,}<extra></extra>') %>%
    fx_plot_layout(y_title = "Total Weekday Rail Station Boardings",
                   filename = "cta_rail_boardings_by_ccvi")
}

# function for plotting weekday boardings by month and station line; lines is a
# list of line names (e.g., c("Blue", "Red")), all lines by default
fx_plot_ridership_by_line <- function(rail_stations_ccvi_ridership, lines = names(pal_line)) {
  ridership_by_line <- rail_stations_ccvi_ridership %>%
    filter(station_line %in% lines) %>%
    group_by(year_month, station_line) %>%
    summarise(rides_total = sum(rides_total), .groups = "drop")

  plot_ly(data = ridership_by_line,
          x = ~year_month,
          y = ~rides_total,
          type = 'scatter',
          mode = 'lines',
          color = ~station_line,
          colors = pal_line,
          text = ~station_line,
          hovertemplate = '%{text}: %{y:,}<extra></extra>') %>%
    fx_plot_layout(y_title = "Total Weekday Rail Station Boardings",
                   filename = "cta_rail_boardings_by_line")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ridershipbyccvi
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Weekday Rail Boardings by CTA L Station CCVI Category, Chicago, Illinois, January 1999-", format(ridership_through, "%B %Y"))

# plot weekday rail boardings per month by station CCVI category
fx_plot_ridership_by_ccvi(rail_stations_ccvi_ridership)

```

# Step 5. Map of stations and ridership by L line
The final step is to create a custom map that displays changes in ridership by station for the rail lines you selected for further analysis. Stations shown in red have lost ridership between `r format(ridership_through, "%B")` 2019 (before the pandemic) and `r format(ridership_through, "%B %Y")` (the latest month available). Comparing the same month in both years keeps seasonal differences in ridership out of the comparison. Larger circles indicate larger percentage changes. Hover over specific stations to display ridership numbers for the analyzed period as well as the net and percentage changes. Turn on the "CCVI Category" layer in the upper right to compare changes in ridership with community vulnerability. Copy and paste the map into your presentation.

```{r}
#| label: define station change functions
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show the station change functions"

# function for calculating the change in weekday boardings by station between
# two months (from and to, as "YYYY-MM-DD"); to is the latest month by default and
# from is the same month in 2019 (before the pandemic) by default, so both months
# are in the same season. Only stations on the selected lines are kept.
fx_station_change <- function(ridership_attributes, rail_stations, lines = names(pal_line),
                              from = NULL, to = NULL) {
  to <- if (is.null(to)) max(ridership_attributes$year_month) else as.Date(to)
  from <- if (is.null(from)) lubridate::make_date(2019, lubridate::month(to), 1) else as.Date(from)

  ridership_attributes %>%
    filter(day_type == "Weekday", year_month %in% c(from, to)) %>%
    group_by(station_id) %>%
    summarise(rides_from = sum(rides_total[year_month == from]),
              rides_to = sum(rides_total[year_month == to]),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(net_chg = rides_to - rides_from,
           pct_chg = net_chg / rides_from * 100,
           month_from = from,
           month_to = to) %>%
    filter(is.finite(pct_chg)) %>%
    inner_join(rail_stations %>%
                 select(station_id, station_name, station_line, comarea_id, comarea_name),
               by = "station_id") %>%
    st_as_sf() %>%
    st_transform(crs = 4326) %>%
    filter(station_line %in% lines)
}

# function for mapping the change in boardings by station along with the selected
# lines; stations that lost riders are red and stations that gained riders are
# blue, with larger circles for larger percentage changes. The layer control turns
# the lines, stations and community area CCVI categories (hidden when the map
# opens) on and off.
fx_map_station_change <- function(station_change, rail_lines, community_areas_ccvi,
                                  lines = names(pal_line)) {
  map_data <- st_transform(community_areas_ccvi, crs = 4326)
  month_from <- format(station_change$month_from[1], "%b %Y")
  month_to <- format(station_change$month_to[1], "%b %Y")
  change_colors <- c(Loss = "#d7301f", Gain = "#2171b5")

  # station hover labels
  station_labels <- sprintf(
    "<strong>%s Station</strong><br/>
    <i>Line:</i> %s<br/>
    <i>Community area:</i> %s<br/>
    <i>%s weekday boardings:</i> %s<br/>
    <i>%s weekday boardings:</i> %s<br/>
    <i>Net change:</i> %s<br/>
    <i>Percent change:</i> %0.1f%%<br/>",
    station_change$station_name,
    station_change$station_line,
    station_change$comarea_name,
    month_from, format(station_change$rides_from, big.mark = ","),
    month_to, format(station_change$rides_to, big.mark = ","),
    format(station_change$net_chg, big.mark = ","),
    station_change$pct_chg) %>%
    lapply(htmltools::HTML)

  ccvi_pal <- colorFactor(palette = "YlOrRd", domain = map_data$`CCVI Category`, ordered = TRUE)

  fx_basemap(map_data) %>%
    addPolygons(
      data = map_data,
      fillColor = ~ccvi_pal(`CCVI Category`),
      label = fx_ccvi_labels(map_data),
      weight = 2,
      opacity = 1,
      color = "white",
      dashArray = "3",
      fillOpacity = 0.5,
      group = "CCVI Category") %>%
    addLegend("bottomleft",
              pal = ccvi_pal,
              values = map_data$`CCVI Category`,
              title = "CCVI Category",
              opacity = 1,
              group = "CCVI Category") %>%
    fx_add_rail_layers(filter(rail_lines, COLOR %in% lines),
                       station_change,
                       station_labels,
                       radius = rescale(abs(station_change$pct_chg), to = c(4, 12)),
                       fillColor = unname(change_colors[if_else(station_change$pct_chg < 0, "Loss", "Gain")])) %>%
    addLegend("bottomleft",
              colors = unname(change_colors),
              labels = c("Loss", "Gain"),
              title = paste0("Change in Weekday Boardings<br>", month_from, " to ", month_to),
              opacity = 0.9,
              className = "info legend circle-legend",
              group = "L Stations") %>%
    addLayersControl(
      overlayGroups = c("L Lines", "L Stations", "CCVI Category"),
      options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE, position = "topright")) %>%
    hideGroup("CCVI Category")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-selectstations
#| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Change in Weekday Ridership by L Station, ", format(ridership_through, "%B"), " 2019-", format(ridership_through, "%Y"))

# calculate the change in weekday boardings by station for the selected lines,
# between the latest month and the same month in 2019
ridership_attributes_station <- fx_station_change(ridership_attributes, 
                                                  rail_stations, 
                                                  lines = a_station_line_list)

# map the change in boardings by station and the selected lines
fx_map_station_change(ridership_attributes_station, 
                      rail_lines, 
                      community_areas_ccvi, 
                      lines = a_station_line_list)

```
